title: Section separation characterizes a conservative family of points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and let $\{p_i:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of points [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For each $i$, let $u_i:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ be the functor $u_i(U)=p_i^{-1}(h_U^\#)$, where $h_U=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,U)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and identify $p_i^{-1}\mathcal F$ with its stalk $\mathcal F_{p_i}=\varinjlim_{(U,x)}\mathcal F(U)$; write $[U,x,t]_{p_i}$ for the class represented by $x\in u_i(U)$ and $t\in\mathcal F(U)$. If for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$, every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, and every pair $s\ne s'$ in $\mathcal F(U)$ there are $i\in I$ and $x\in u_i(U)$ with $[U,x,s]_{p_i}\ne[U,x,s']_{p_i}$, then the inverse-image functors $p_i^{-1}$ jointly reflect isomorphisms of sheaves: whenever every $p_i^{-1}(a)$ is a bijection, a morphism $a$ is an isomorphism.
